bean_snapshot.name: Tanzania Peaberry
bean_snapshot.notes: Altitude range 1100–1700 masl. Harvest window May–December 2026.

intent: first roast of a new bean - establish a baseline for Tanzania Peaberry

adjustments.reason: full caramelization aroma, full cinnamon color, silverskin beginning to peel

sensory.aroma_drying: toasted bread at 2:30, beans still green; toasted bread again at 5:00 as color started to change
sensory.aroma_maillard: lightly roasted peanuts at 7:00; caramel malt at 8:30; full caramelization at 10:00
sensory.aroma_development: full roast smell at 15:00 as first crack began
sensory.color_at_yellowing: browning/yellowing at 7:00 with beans plumping; dark popcorn kernel color at 8:30; full cinnamon at 10:00
sensory.color_at_drop: notably dark - darker than the 12.8% weight loss and 60s development would predict
sensory.crack_character: first crack onset 15:00, end 19:00 - 4:00 of crack
sensory.observations: Timer counted down from 18:00; elapsed times derived as 18:00 minus remaining, so notes logged past 0:00 (-1:00, -2:00) are 19:00 and 20:00 elapsed. Silverskin began peeling at 10:00 and was peeling again at 19:00. Dropped to cooldown at 20:00, cooling ran to 26:00 elapsed (6 min). Green weight 250.95g is marginally over the CB-101's 250g rated capacity. Post-roast assessment: color came out considerably darker than target and the cooled beans carry a faint smoke note, despite weight loss (12.8%) and development time (60s) both landing in the light-roast band and no second crack. roast_level_achieved recorded as light on the strength of the moisture and development numbers; the dark surface color reads as a bake artifact from the 20:00 total time rather than a genuinely darker roast. Pending visual check for tipped beans to rule out scorch.
